name: Simeon
overview: Simeon is a male figure in Scripture, known as the second-born son of Jacob and Leah and the eponymous ancestor of the tribe of Simeon. His identity is closely tied to his tribal affiliation and his birth order among Jacob's sons.
namesAndTitles: The name Simeon means 'he has heard' in Hebrew, as recorded in Genesis 29:33. This proper name was not given directly by God but reflects the circumstances of his birth.
familyAndRelationships: Simeon is the son of Jacob and Leah, making him a full brother to Reuben, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun, and Dinah. He also had several half-brothers, including Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, and Joseph. Notably, he was involved in a violent family conflict resulting in the deaths of Shechem and Hamor.
scriptureSignificance: Simeon's role in the biblical narrative is marked by his participation with Levi in avenging their sister Dinah, an act that brought familial and divine condemnation. Later in the story, Simeon was detained in Egypt by his brother Joseph, serving as a guarantee for the family's return with Benjamin. His tribe was eventually integrated into Judah's territory, and his descendants became known for their zeal in defending Israel.
